name: Isolated Gallbladder Duplication

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Radiologic and Surgical Identification Criteria for Gallbladder Duplication

criteria.description: Identification of two distinct gallbladder structures on imaging modalities such as ultrasound, MRCP, or CT scan
Intraoperative confirmation of two separate gallbladders with independent cystic ducts
Absence of other biliary or hepatic congenital anomalies to confirm isolated duplication

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of two distinct gallbladder structures confirmed by imaging or surgery with exclusion of other biliary anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often incidental during imaging or surgery; awareness is critical to avoid surgical complications.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Visualization of two separate gallbladder lumens on imaging
searchTerms: two gallbladder chambers seen on scan

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of two cystic ducts draining separately into the biliary tree
searchTerms: two separate bile ducts draining gallbladder
dual cystic ducts entering bile system

common.notes: May be related to cholelithiasis or cholecystitis

occasional.symptomName: Gallstone formation in one or both gallbladders
searchTerms: stones in one or both gallbladders

occasional.symptomName: Biliary colic triggered by fatty meals
searchTerms: biliary colic triggered by greasy meals

rare.symptomName: Cholangitis secondary to bile duct obstruction
searchTerms: bile duct infection due to blockage

rare.symptomName: Pancreatitis due to biliary sludge or stones
searchTerms: pancreatitis caused by gallstones or sludge

laboratory: Elevated alkaline phosphatase and bilirubin in obstructive cases
imaging: Ultrasound showing two separate gallbladder structures
Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) demonstrating duplicated gallbladder and cystic ducts
genetic: No known specific genetic mutations identified
other: Intraoperative identification of two gallbladders with separate cystic ducts
Histopathological confirmation of gallbladder tissue in both structures

distinguishingFeatures: Cystic dilatation of bile ducts rather than duplicated gallbladder
Identified on imaging as a fold rather than duplication

redFlags: Recurrent biliary colic despite prior cholecystectomy
Postoperative bile leak or biliary injury
references: Kelley SR, et al. Gallbladder duplication: a review of anatomy and clinical implications. J Gastrointest Surg. 2020.
Sarin SK, et al. Imaging of biliary tract anomalies. Radiol Clin North Am. 2019.
